title: Under `nvs run`, `[limits] wall_time` and `max_output` are parsed and never stop the program.
text: `rule:errors/on-limit` lists `max_output` and wall time beside memory and CPU time as limit `FATAL`s, `rule:config/no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration` gives `wall_time` no default but no exemption for a CLI run, and `rule:config/an-application-is-its-entry-file-path` writes `wall_time = "600s"` for an `[[app]] entry` that is an `nvs run` script. Under `nvs run` with `[limits] wall_time = "1s"`, a `Core\Time::sleep(5s)` ends normally after 5 s and a `while (true)` loop runs until it is killed; with `max_output = "10"`, a loop that echoes 11 bytes a thousand times writes all 11000. The run registers with the watchdog for the CPU ceiling alone (`crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs:3681`), and nothing in `crates/nvs-cli/src` reads `wall_time`: the runtime publishes it into the tree's state (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/safepoint.rs:89`), where the server's disconnect grace is its reader (`crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs:1250`). The output ceiling is read into the context (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/limits.rs:558`) and compared only inside `nvs_safepoint` (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/safepoint.rs:756`), which compiled code enters only when the safepoint word is non-zero, and a write charges the counter without raising a flag (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/output.rs:286`). Whether `nvs serve` enforces either limit is not checked. Closing it means a run arms a deadline from `wall_time` that expires the safepoint word, a write that crosses `max_output` raises a flag the next poll reads, and a conformance case pins each `FATAL` with its limit report.
